en: The loss stays with you, and the records stay with whoever decided. But a digital service cannot change in just any way, and when it crosses the line someone answers for it.

Depending on the case, the request may include access to the conversation history and its minimum records, a sufficient explanation of the limits that matter and clarity about changes in how the service is used. The aim is to be able to link what was promised to the effect you suffered.

If the punishment has no verifiable reason or reasonable path of challenge, the request can be that it be reviewed or undone. Along with that, the company can be required to state which punishment it applied and for what reason, and to offer a path of challenge that works.
The offer can also be corrected and fulfilled, and the communication that does not match reality, stopped.

The first response is for the function to come back. The request may include undoing the change, when technically feasible, or replacing the item with another that plays the same role, as well as correcting the way the update was made.
The company must also state what changed, when, for what reason and with what effect on the item. And compensation in money remains possible when restoring is not feasible or not enough.

When no individual, consistent evidence rules out your good faith, the request can be that the removed items come back and that your account be restored. The company can be called on to keep and show the records and to explain why the measure hit you in particular.

It is also worth demanding minimum clarity about the moderation criteria, the review of what can stay online, and about the criteria for distributing what appears. This does not oblige the network to open its internal systems, but it must be enough to understand how the decision affected you and to challenge it.
The request can be that the company correct the way it informs, put what matters in view and show what it actually displayed to you. And what you lost because of the lack of clarity can be restored.

The request may include that the app keep and show the minimum records, explain the restrictions verifiably and review the criteria used to restrict, with clarity about what defines the distribution of calls and the restoration of what the change made worse.

The request may include minimum clarity about the criteria that decide the order of offers and about the preference the platform gives to some of them. It also covers control of changes that lower your position without excluding you and close attention to the use of the data it collects when intermediating sales.
